messages.author: a117157461b73acc
messages.subject: five Likert scale data that are not distributed in a normal distribution
parts:
Hi
I have five Likert scale data that are not distributed in a normal distribution. Is there a method by Lavaan that can be converted to a normal distribution?
I noticed that some researchers use symmetric and non-symmetric thresholds. I don’t know if it is one of the ways to transform the data into a normal distribution and how that is in Lavaan

messages.subject: Re: five Likert scale data that are not distributed in a normal distribution
parts:
Although this is often (rightly) discussed critically, you could consider scales with 5 points as continuous and use MLR. A transformation of the data makes little sense. Pat has already noted this.

Am 20.12.20, 00:58 schrieb "Patrick (Malone Quantitative)" <mal...@malonequantitative.com>:

The probit regression that lavaan uses with ordered data (outcomes or indicators) assumes an underlying normal distribution that is coarsely measured, at various cutpoints reflected by the thresholds.
